steps.title: Prepare your own matching disc with the project’s tools
steps.instruction: Use an independently permitted complete The Urbz: Sims in the City original-Xbox Windows player, separate from any desktop, handheld or other console edition. Supply your own USA disc ISO/xiso or complete extracted game tree with default.xbe and all matching assets/movies. This title’s documented default.xbe is 3,035,136 bytes, SHA-1 5712b6a3e2eaaacfcae228cf6154ade499a0033c, title ID 0x45410060; another revision is not interchangeable. The runtime compares the loaded XBE with its own compiled expected hash; a matching executable does not authenticate every disc byte. Complete extraction or supported compilation upstream; no original, BIOS, compiler or helper is obtained or run by Portcove.

steps.title: Select the completed game player
steps.instruction: Select Urbz.exe, with its complete creating player directory as working directory and no arguments for normal launch. Keep its matching runtime DLLs, resources, notices and assets/ together. The Windows route uses Direct3D 12 and XAudio2; keep the supported host graphics/runtime dependencies installed upstream. The source locates assets/ beside the executable or in ancestor folders; preserve the actual selected tree rather than redirecting originals during attachment. Do not select build scripts, generators or another title’s executable.

steps.title: Close every game process before maintenance
steps.instruction: The Windows player runs the game in its own process, but an Xbox title reboot can start a separate executable. Portcove does not track that successor as part of this registration; this guide does not establish when this title uses it. Close the actual game and all companions before changing files or adding another copy. Registration status alone does not show that every process has stopped.

steps.title: Review launch details, then choose Play
steps.instruction: Review and consent to the selected executable, working folder and launch arguments, then choose Play separately. You and the project manage setup, version changes, recovery and all external files. Removing the registration leaves those files in place. Before changing versions, close every game process and keep the complete working player and all its data. Review and select the executable again if its files change. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, migration or deletion for this external copy.
